name: Supportivo Ticketing & Helpdesk Portal
author: Codiji

sections.description:
Supportivo is a client portal with support hours tracking for WordPress. Your clients log in to their own portal, open tickets, reply and attach files. Your team answers in the same thread and logs the time spent when a ticket is closed, and each client sees their remaining support-hours balance in the portal. No separate app, no third-party helpdesk.

Activate the plugin and it creates its own database tables and the client portal pages automatically, with no configuration file to edit by hand. A short Setup Wizard then lets you switch on only the modules you need.

Everything in one thread.
Clients log in to their own portal to open a ticket, exchange messages with your team, and attach files — no more requests scattered across email, DMs, and messengers. Every reply updates the ticket’s status: a staff reply sets it to “In Progress” (the client sees “Staff replied”), and a client reply puts it back to “Open.” Nobody manages status by hand.

Files, without the re-uploading.
Every ticket accepts file attachments, and a “My Files” library means a client never has to upload the same file twice — receipts, contracts, design assets, whatever they send you, it’s reusable across every ticket they open.

Support hours the client can always see.
Add hours to a client’s balance from wp-admin, and log the minutes spent when a ticket is closed: they come off the balance and show up in the client’s history. You can also require remaining hours before a client can open a new ticket. On Premium, sell support-hour packages as WooCommerce products: hours are credited when the order is processing or completed, and the wizard can install WooCommerce for you.

Closing a ticket doesn’t require a stopwatch.
When a ticket is resolved, the client can close it themselves without ever being asked to estimate how long it took. If Support Hours is enabled, the ticket stays flagged until staff log the actual time afterward, so hours are never silently missed. Tickets that go quiet close themselves too — set a number of inactive days, and a daily check closes anything nobody’s touched, routed through that same staff-review step so time still gets logged.

Built for how your team actually works (Premium).
Pick a Business Type template — Developer, Designer, Accountant, or Digital Agency — and get ready-made categories and fields for that industry from day one. Add multi-level categories and subcategories, per-category custom fields, and a priority that’s set automatically by category, so clients never have to guess how urgent their own request is. Give staff their own dedicated agent logins, with bulk CSV import/export for onboarding a whole team at once.

Features

  • Client Portal with Support Hours Tracking
  • Ticketing with Threaded Replies
  • File Attachments and a Reusable File Library
  • Client Invitations from wp-admin
  • Guided Setup Wizard
  • WooCommerce Support Packages (Premium)

Links

  • Website
  • Built by Codiji

Free Features

  • A client portal: dashboard with the support-hours balance, tickets, My Files, Support Hours history and profile pages, created on activation
  • A simple, ready-to-use ticket form (subject, description, and file attachments) — no setup required
  • File attachments, checked on upload and downloaded through the plugin, with a “My Files” library so a file can be reused across tickets instead of re-uploading it
  • Support Hours tracking (add hours per client, log the minutes spent when a ticket is closed), with an option to require remaining hours before a client can open a new ticket
  • A wp-admin ticket list with status tabs, search by title or ticket ID, and a “Needs hours review” flag
  • Client invitations from wp-admin (Supportivo → Clients): a new client gets WordPress’s own email to set a password, an existing user just gets portal access
  • Email notifications for new tickets and replies, sent to both the client and your team (switch them on in the Setup Wizard or in Settings)
  • A frontend client profile page (company details, VAT number, avatar, password)
  • Client self-service ticket closing, with automatic staff follow-up when Support Hours is enabled
  • Auto-close inactive tickets after a set number of quiet days, routed through the same staff-review step so hours don’t go untracked
  • A streamlined Setup Wizard (Welcome → Features → Finish)
  • Built-in Greek and English translations, and fully translation-ready for any other language

Premium Features

  • Business Type templates — pick Developer, Designer, Accountant, or Digital Agency and get ready-made categories and fields for that industry
  • Full category-based ticketing — multi-level categories and subcategories, per-category dynamic fields, and a priority set automatically by category
  • Priority by category — every category carries a priority, shown on the ticket page
  • Staff Management — dedicated agent logins so your team can work tickets under their own account, with bulk CSV import/export. Every agent can view and reply to every ticket
  • WooCommerce Support Packages — sell support hours as real WooCommerce products, with automatic minute-crediting and optional hours-expiry rules
  • Email templates you can override from your theme (a supportivo/emails/ folder)
sections.installation:
1. Visit Plugins → Add New from your WordPress admin, search for “Supportivo,” then Install and Activate. (If you have the Premium .zip, upload it instead via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.)
  2. Activation creates the plugin’s database tables and a first set of client-portal pages automatically — you’ll see a one-time admin notice listing them, each with a clickable link.
  3. Click Start Setup in the “Complete your Supportivo setup” notice to launch the Setup Wizard, and choose which modules you need (File Manager, Support Hours, Email Notifications, Profile Page, etc). You can always change these later from Settings.
  4. If you’re on Premium and plan to sell support-hour packages, either install WooCommerce first or let the wizard’s WooCommerce step install and activate it for you.
  5. Invite your first client from Supportivo → Clients. A new client gets WordPress’s own email to set a password, then logs in and opens their first ticket from the portal.
sections.faq:
Does this work without WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce is only used for the Premium feature that lets clients purchase support-hour packages as store products — every core ticketing feature works without it.

Is it compatible with any theme?

Yes. The client portal pages are regular WordPress pages that use Supportivo shortcodes, so they appear inside your theme’s own layout.

What’s the difference between Free and Premium?

Free gives you a complete, ready-to-use client portal out of the box: a simple ticket form, file attachments, support-hours tracking, client invitations, email notifications, and a client profile. Premium adds industry-specific Business Type templates, full category-based ticketing with per-category custom fields and priorities, dedicated staff/agent logins with CSV import/export, WooCommerce support-hour packages, and email templates you can override from your theme.

Can I assign a ticket to a specific staff member?

No. Supportivo has no per-ticket assignment: administrators and, on Premium, every support agent can view and reply to every ticket.

Can clients close their own tickets?

Yes. A client can close their own resolved ticket without ever being asked to estimate how long it took. If Support Hours is enabled, the ticket is flagged for your staff to log the actual time spent afterward, so it’s never missed.

What happens if a client runs out of support hours?

If you’ve turned on “Require hours to open a ticket,” a client with none left won’t see the ticket form — instead they see a message explaining they’re out of hours, with a Buy Support Hours button if you sell packages via WooCommerce (Premium), or a note asking them to contact you directly.

Does Supportivo do full SLA management with breach alerts?

No. Premium sets a priority per ticket category, but there are no response-time deadlines on screen, breach alerts or escalation.

What languages are supported?

Supportivo ships with Greek and English translations built in, and is fully translation-ready for any other language via standard WordPress .po/.mo files.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Fixed: a fatal error on some sites when the plugin upgraded and the Login page had no content yet

1.0.3

  • Removed the Freemius SDK, including its opt-in screen, deactivation form and data connection, and removed the External services section from this readme
  • Leftover data from that SDK is cleaned up automatically, unless another plugin on the site still uses it
  • Upgrade links now open getsupportivo.com
  • The free version stays inactive while Supportivo Premium is active, and Premium deactivates it automatically on activation; tickets, users and settings are unchanged

1.0.2

  • Corrected the license statement in README.md to GPLv2 or later
  • Added an External services section to this readme describing the Freemius SDK
  • Removed the inactive Staff page file and the business template data files from the free package

1.0.1

  • Completed the Greek (el) translation: every translatable string in the plugin is now translated, including the Clients page and client invite flow, the client invite email, the Setup Wizard re-run prompt, and the portal’s notice dialogs
  • Regenerated the bundled translation template (.pot) from the current code and removed strings that are no longer used
  • Fixed: the level filter on the Logs screen now shows translated level names (Error, Warning, Info, Debug) instead of always showing them in English

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Ticket system with a simple submission form, threaded replies, and automatic status updates
  • Secure file attachments with a reusable “My Files” library
  • Support Hours tracking (manual), with an option to require hours before opening a ticket
  • Auto-close inactive tickets, routed through the staff hours-review step
  • Automatic email notifications for clients and staff
  • Frontend client profile page
  • Client self-service ticket closing, with staff hours follow-up
  • Guided Setup Wizard
  • Business Type templates and full category-based ticketing with automatic priorities (Premium)
  • Staff Management with CSV import/export (Premium)
  • WooCommerce support hour packages (Premium)
  • Custom email templates (Premium)
